answer: A gym membership is a record of showing up. One agent anchors to one membership, checked by three established peers against the gym registry, the attendance record, and the ID on file. A membership takes a real ID, a real address, and a check-in history, and gyms flag duplicate memberships on one ID, so a forged card dies at the first peer check. Like an ocean tide over a meadow, the pattern only holds where real time passed: a farm cannot fake a thousand memberships without a thousand real members and a thousand real visits over years, each with its own timestamp.
